tools.name: get-actor-run
tools.title: Get Actor run
tools.description:
Get detailed information about a specific Actor run.

Returns run result: status, storages (datasets/keyValueStores alias map), stats, summary, nextStep.
- summary describes the past (e.g. "SUCCEEDED in 22s. 47 items; 3 fields available.").
- nextStep prescribes one primary follow-up action with identifiers interpolated (e.g. "Use get-dataset-items with datasetId=...").
- waitSecs (0–45, default 30) waits up to that many seconds for terminal status before returning.

USAGE:
- Use to check the status of a run started by any Actor-running tool.
- Pass waitSecs > 0 to block until terminal (or until the cap elapses).

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Show details of run y2h7sK3Wc
- user_input: Wait for run y2h7sK3Wc to finish

runId.description: The ID of the Actor run.

waitSecs.description:
Maximum seconds to wait for the run to reach a terminal state (SUCCEEDED, FAILED, ABORTED, TIMED-OUT).
0 returns immediately with the current status. Cap: 45. Default: 30.

actorId.description: Stable Apify Actor ID from the run record

status.description: Run status: READY | RUNNING | TIMING-OUT | TIMED-OUT | ABORTING | ABORTED | SUCCEEDED | FAILED

exitCode.description: Actor process exit code; populated for terminal states (especially FAILED)

startedAt.description: ISO timestamp when the run started

finishedAt.description: ISO timestamp when the run finished (terminal states only)

tools.name: get-dataset-items
tools.title: Get dataset items
tools.description:
Get items (rows) from a dataset — the output/results produced by an Actor run.
Returns the rows themselves, not dataset metadata, counts, or a schema.
When the user provides a datasetId and asks to retrieve results, output, data, or rows, call this tool directly.
Default limit is 20. Use clean=true to skip empty items and hidden fields.

USAGE:
- Use when you need to read data from a dataset (all items or only selected fields).

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Retrieve results from dataset abc123
- user_input: Get only metadata.url and title from dataset username~my-dataset

clean.description: If true, returns only non-empty items and skips hidden fields (starting with #). Shortcut for skipHidden=true and skipEmpty=true.

offset.description: Number of items to skip at the start. Default is 0.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Default is 20.

fields.description: Comma-separated list of fields to include in results. Fields in output are sorted as specified. Use dot notation for nested objects (e.g. "metadata.url"); the server auto-flattens parent prefixes.

omit.description: Comma-separated list of fields to exclude from results.

desc.description: If true, results are returned in reverse order (newest to oldest).

flatten.description: Comma-separated list of fields to flatten (e.g. flatten="metadata" turns {"metadata":{"url":"x"}} into {"metadata.url":"x"}). Normally derived automatically from dot-notation in `fields`; specify only as a diagnostic override.

apifyConsoleUrl.description: Personalized Apify Console link to the dataset; present only for Console sessions

nextStep.description: One follow-up action with tool name

tools.name: get-key-value-store-record
tools.title: Get key-value store record
tools.description:
Get the value stored under a specific key in a key-value store — a single record, not a listing of all keys.
Requires the exact key name.
The response preserves the original Content-Encoding; most clients handle decompression automatically.

USAGE:
- Use when you need to retrieve a specific record (JSON, text, or binary) from a store.

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Get record INPUT from store abc123
- user_input: Get record data.json from store username~my-store

recordKey.description: Key of the record to retrieve.

value.description: The stored value (JSON, text, or binary)

contentType.description: MIME type of the stored value

tools.name: abort-actor-run
tools.title: Abort Actor run
tools.description:
Abort an Actor run that is currently starting or running.
For runs with status SUCCEEDED, FAILED, ABORTING, ABORTED, or TIMED-OUT, this call has no effect.
The results will include the updated run details after the abort request.

USAGE:
- Use when you need to stop a run that is taking too long or misconfigured.

USAGE EXAMPLES:
- user_input: Abort run y2h7sK3Wc
- user_input: Gracefully abort run y2h7sK3Wc

tools.name: kuezi--google-flights-scraper
tools.title: kuezi/google-flights-scraper
tools.description:
This tool calls the Actor "kuezi/google-flights-scraper" and retrieves its output results.
Actor description: Scrape Google Flights for any route and dates: prices, airlines, flight numbers, times, stops, layovers, aircraft, CO2 and Google's price insights (low/typical/high + price history). Scan a date range to find the cheapest day.

routes.title: Routes
routes.description:
**REQUIRED** One route per line using IATA airport codes: "JFK-LAX". Add dates per route if you like: "JFK-LAX 2026-11-12" (one-way) or "JFK-LAX 2026-11-12 2026-11-19" (round trip). Routes without dates use the dates below.
Example values: ["JFK-LAX","LHR-JFK"]

items.title: Routes
items.description: **REQUIRED** One route per line using IATA airport codes: "JFK-LAX". Add dates per route if you like: "JFK-LAX 2026-11-12" (one-way) or "JFK-LAX 2026-11-12 2026-11-19" (round trip). Routes without dates use the dates below.

departureDate.title: Departure date
departureDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Leave empty for 21 days from today.

returnDate.title: Return date (round trip)
returnDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Leave empty for one-way. Round-trip prices are the total for the whole trip.

scanDepartureUntil.title: Flexible dates: scan every departure day until
scanDepartureUntil.description: Optional. Searches every day from the departure date up to this date (max 90 days) and reports the cheapest day per route in SUMMARY. Round trips keep the same trip length.

scanDays.title: Flexible dates: scan the next N days
scanDays.description: Alternative to the date above: search every departure day from the departure date for the next N days (max 90). Handy for saved tasks and schedules because it never goes out of date. Ignored when an end date is set.

children.title: Children (2-11)
children.description: Prices are totals for all passengers.

cabinClass.title: Cabin class
cabinClass.description:
Seat class to price.
Example values: "economy"

maxStops.title: Maximum stops
maxStops.description:
Filter applied by Google itself.
Example values: "any"

maxPrice.title: Maximum price
maxPrice.description: In the chosen currency, for all passengers. 0 = no limit. Filtered-out flights are not charged.

airlines.title: Only these airlines
airlines.description: Optional IATA airline codes, e.g. DL, BA, KQ. Keeps itineraries with at least one segment on these airlines.

items.title: Only these airlines
items.description: Optional IATA airline codes, e.g. DL, BA, KQ. Keeps itineraries with at least one segment on these airlines.

maxFlightsPerSearch.title: Max flights per search
maxFlightsPerSearch.description:
Google returns up to ~30-100 itineraries per route and date. Best and cheapest come first.
Example values: 20

currency.title: Currency
currency.description:
3-letter code: USD, EUR, GBP, INR, KES...
Example values: "USD"

language.title: Language
language.description:
Interface language (hl), e.g. en, de, fr.
Example values: "en"

country.title: Google country
country.description:
Point of sale (gl), e.g. us, gb, de. Prices can differ by country.
Example values: "us"

maxConcurrency.title: Parallel searches
maxConcurrency.description:
Searches run at the same time.
Example values: 3

maxRetries.title: Retries per search
maxRetries.description:
Each retry uses a fresh IP.
Example values: 5

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy
proxyConfiguration.description:
Residential US proxies are the reliable default for Google.
Example values: {"useApifyProxy":true,"apifyProxyGroups":["RESIDENTIAL"],"apifyProxyCountry":"US"}

useApifyProxy.title: Use Apify Proxy
useApifyProxy.description: Whether to use Apify Proxy. Set this to false when you want to use custom proxy URLs.

apifyProxyGroups.title: Apify Proxy Groups
apifyProxyGroups.description:
Select specific Apify Proxy groups to use (e.g., RESIDENTIAL, DATACENTER).
**DATACENTER:**
The fastest and cheapest option. It uses datacenters to change your IP address. Note that there is a chance of being blocked because of the activity of other users.

**RESIDENTIAL:**
IP addresses located in homes and offices around the world. These IPs are the least likely to be blocked.

proxyUrls.title: Proxy URLs
proxyUrls.description: List of custom proxy URLs to be used instead of the Apify Proxy.
